'''Saturday Night's Main Event I''' was a [[professional wrestling]] [[television special]] produced by the [[World Wrestling Federation]] (WWF). The event took place on May 10, 1985 at the [[Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum]] in [[Uniondale, New York]] and aired on tape delay the following night on [[NBC]].

==Production==
===Background===
On July 23, 1984 and February 18, 1985, the WWF had aired two live television specials titled ''[[The Brawl to End it All]]'' and ''[[The War to Settle the Score]]'' on [[MTV]] with ''The War to Settle the Score'' serving as a prelude to the inaugural [[WrestleMania I|WrestleMania]] event.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> | title=Historical Cards: WrestleMania I (03-31-1985) | magazine=PWI 2007 Wrestling Almanac & Book of facts | location= Blue Bell, Pennsylvania | publisher= [[London Publishing]] | date=June 2007 | editor-first=Harry | editor-last=Burkett | page=84 | isbn=978-25274-00389}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wwf/misctv.html#war|title=The War to Settle the Score results|publisher=Wrestling Supercards and Tournaments|access-date=2010-09-05|date=February 18, 1985}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wwf/misctv.html#brawl|title=The War to Settle the Score results|publisher=Wrestling Supercards and Tournaments|access-date=2010-09-05|date=July 23, 1984}}</ref> Following a [[Saturday Night Live]] episode which took place on the night before WrestleMania which featured [[Hulk Hogan]] and [[Mr. T]] as last-minute replacement hosts for the episode,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/every-athlete-who-has-hosted-saturday-night-live|title=All 36 athletes who have hosted 'Saturday Night Live'|first=Gabbi|last=Shaw|date=September 26, 2026|publisher=Business Insider}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/hulk-hogan-snl-mrt-monologue-wrestled-heckler|title=Hulk Hogan & Mr. T Wrestled a Heckler During Their 1985 SNL Monologue|first=Lauren|last=Piester|date=July 25, 2025|publisher=[[NBC]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite episode|title=Hulk Hogan, Mr. T, and The Commodores|episode-link=List of Saturday Night Live episodes#1980s| series=Saturday Night Live|series-link =Saturday Night Live|network=NBC|season=10|number=193}}</ref> then-SNL producer [[Dick Ebersol]] met with [[Vince McMahon|Vince]] and [[Linda McMahon]]. In the meeting, Ebersol and the McMahons agreed to a 50-50 split on production fees which resulted in Ebersol and Vince getting sent half of the fees that were sent from NBC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.postwrestling.com/2024/12/12/the-return-of-saturday-nights-main-event-40-years-later/|title=The Return of Saturday Night’s Main Event – 40 Years Later|first=John|last=Pollock|date=December 12, 2024|publisher=POST Wrestling}}</ref> Prior to the taping, Ebersol and the WWF employed higher production standards for the event including multiple cameras with boom microphones and concert-quality sound.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Sex, Lies, and Headlocks: The Real Story of Vince McMahon and World Wrestling Entertainment|date=July 16, 2002
|first1=Assael|last1=Shaun|first2=Mike|last2=Mooneyham|publisher=Crown Publishing Group}}</ref>

===Storylines===
The event included four matches that resulted from scripted storylines. Results were predetermined by the WWF's writers.<ref>{{cite web|title=How Pro Wrestling Works|url=https://entertainment.howstuffworks.com/pro-wrestling.htm|last=Grabianowski|first=Ed|date=January 13, 2006|work=HowStuffWorks|publisher=[[Discovery Communications]]|access-date=March 5, 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131129050844/https://entertainment.howstuffworks.com/pro-wrestling.htm|archive-date=November 29, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Live & Televised Entertainment|url=https://corporate.wwe.com/company/events.jsp|work=[[WWE]]|access-date=March 21, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218142749/https://corporate.wwe.com/company/events.jsp|archive-date=February 18, 2009}}</ref> while storylines were produced on the WWF's weekly television shows, ''[[Prime Time Wrestling]]'', ''[[Tuesday Night Titans]]'', ''[[WWF Championship Wrestling|Championship Wrestling]]'', and [[WWF All-Star Wrestling|All-Star Wrestling]].
===Aftermath===
When the event had aired, the event drew an 8.8 rating which prompted [[NBC]] to order more specials for the network in periods where SNL did not air beginning with [[Saturday Night's Main Event II]] which aired on October 3, 1985.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=2985|title=WWF Saturday Night's Main Event #1 « Events Database « CAGEMATCH - The Internet Wrestling Database|website=www.cagematch.net|access-date=2019-09-17|archive-date=October 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201006053358/https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=2985|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Saturday Night's Main Event #2|work=Pro Wrestling History|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wwf/snme.html#2|access-date=2007-10-05|archive-date=August 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809183006/http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wwf/snme.html#2|url-status=live}}</ref>
